verdicts.reason: A keeps the original left-to-right order, but the logo badge is oversized: it fills almost the full height, crowds the top and bottom edges and pulls focus from the headline. The CTA also sits tight to the right edge. B uses the same structure with a slightly smaller logo and better side margins on the CTA. Its weakness is the large empty gap between the subline and the CTA.

A keeps the banner's left-to-right flow, but the logo is oversized and dominates the headline, and the CTA is close to the right edge. B stacks the headline, subline and CTA in a column next to the logo. That leaves the right ~40% of the canvas empty and makes the layout lopsided, which does not suit a wide banner.

A flips the original order and pushes the logo to the far right edge, leaving a wide empty gap in the middle. The brand no longer leads, and the CTA is stacked under the text instead of reading as the end of the line. B keeps the original logo → message → CTA order, but its oversized logo crowds the canvas height and the CTA sits tight to the right edge.
